subject: Dedicated capacity fit: GPU family selection & $/1M token target — follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mia Chen <mia@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Tyler O'Neal <tyler@cloudwave.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity fit & target $/1M — recap and ask

Hi Mia / Tyler —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap / confirmation so we can align pricing options:

Use case summary:
- Primary: real-time customer support summarization + short-context retrieval for chat (multi-turn).
- Average request: ~512 tokens input + 256 tokens output (peak sequences ~1k).
- Current active users: 120 concurrent chat sessions during peak. Expected growth to 350 in 6–9 months.

Throughput and latency goals:
- Target steady-state throughput: ~3–4M tokens/day initially, moving to ~10M tokens/day in next 6 months (burst to 15M).
- Latency target: 150–250ms p90 for single-turn generation; p99 target acceptable up to 500ms if batching helps unit econ.

Pricing / budget signal: you mentioned wanting to understand dedicated reserved economics and a target $/1M tokens that keeps the deal attractive for CloudWave. Can you confirm a target range for $/1M tokens and an initial commit budget range (monthly)?

Preliminary Redwood guidance (so you know what we'll model):
- GPU families we typically recommend for low-latency production: H100 (best p90/p99) or A100 80GB (cost-focused but still good perf).
- Typical reserved sizing: 2xH100 equivalent for a low-latency pilot; 4xA100 equivalent if prioritizing cost and higher concurrent throughput.

Ask / next steps:
1) Confirm expected steady-state tokens/day (pick a conservative number: 3M vs 4M vs 6M).
2) Confirm target $/1M tokens (range helps us prepare tiered pricing bands).
3) Would you prefer we model a 3-month pilot (convertible to reserved commit) or go straight to a 12-month reserved plan?

I'll put together a short pricing bands spreadsheet and technical assumptions (batching, sequence length, quantization) and loop Camila in to validate throughput assumptions. Attaching a mutual action plan and initial pricing models for your review (stubbed).

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: CW-MutualActionPlan.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_pricing_models.pdf (summary)

From: Mia Chen <mia@cloudwave.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tyler O'Neal <tyler@cloudwave.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity fit & target $/1M — recap and ask

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from our side: 

- Steady-state: expect roughly 4M tokens/day at launch (conservative). If the pilot goes well, we expect to hit ~9–10M/day within 3–4 months.
- Budget / $/1M target: our procurement target is roughly $60–80 per 1M tokens for the committed pricing band. We can consider higher rates for shorter pilots but would need a path below $60 at scale.
- Pilot vs reserve: prefer a 3-month pilot that can convert to a 12-month reserved contract if performance and unit economics check out.

We lean toward lower latency (so H100 is attractive), but we need a clear cost comparison vs A100. Can you send the model with both GPU-family scenarios and the expected unit $/1M tokens for each commit size?

Also cc'ing our ops lead Tyler who will coordinate an infra test window.

Thanks — Mia
Mia Chen
Head of Product, CloudWave Inc
mia@cloudwave.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mia Chen <mia@cloudwave.com>, Tyler O'Neal <tyler@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 13:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity fit & target $/1M — pricing bands attached

Thanks Mia — great, that helps. See attached pricing bands (high level) and assumptions; summary below. I'll leave the technical throughput validation to Camila.

Assumptions used for the model:
- Average sequence length: 768 tokens (512 in + 256 out).
- Effective batching and KV cache reuse reduce token cost by ~18% on steady-state chat patterns.
- We assume non-stop reserved usage during business hours with some burst capacity for peaks; pilot modeled as 12h/day sustained usage with higher bursts.

Estimated unit economics (illustrative):
- Option A — 2x H100 (reserved pilot footprint): estimated $/1M tokens: $55 — $68 (depends on burst hours and quantization). Pros: meets latency targets; fewer GPUs to manage.
- Option B — 4x A100 80GB (reserved): estimated $/1M tokens: $38 — $52. Pros: better raw cost per token at scale; higher concurrent throughput but slightly higher p90 latency vs H100.
- Option C — Hybrid route (1 H100 + 2 A100): estimated $/1M tokens: $45 — $58. Pros: ability to route latency-sensitive traffic to H100 and bulk traffic to A100 to optimize cost/latency tradeoff.

What these ranges include: model hosting, instance-level GPU amortization, baseline IO and NVLink overheads, and a small reserve for autoscaling burst capacity. They do not include one-time onboarding or dedicated security/compliance add-ons (we can add those as line items).

Recommended pilot configuration (what I'd propose we model as a 3-month trial):
- Pilot: 2x H100 reserved for 8 weeks + 30% burst allowance (simple convert-to-reserve path).
- Goals for pilot: validate p90 latency <= 250ms, measure production batching gains (to verify the 18% token reduction), and capture real-world token counts to refine unit pricing for a 12-month commit.

Next steps:
1) Camila: can you validate the sequence-length assumptions and whether the pilot sizing above will meet 4M/day with p90 targets?
2) Mia / Tyler: pick two 60–90 minute slots next week for a pricing + infra test-run deep-dive; I'll share a driven agenda.
3) Marissa / Jordan: we'll prepare a convertible pilot contract that captures the $/1M bands and a path to convert to a 12-month reserved plan.

Attaching: redwood_pricing_models.pdf (detailed bands), CW-MutualActionPlan.xlsx (timeline & checklist).

—Jordan

Attachments: redwood_pricing_models.pdf, CW-MutualActionPlan.xlsx

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mia Chen <mia@cloudwave.com>, Tyler O'Neal <tyler@cloudwave.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jul 2025 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity fit & target $/1M — technical notes

Hi all — quick technical notes to align expectations before the infra test: 

- Sequence and model: assume 1k context support; we recommend serving a quantized LLM variant for chat that preserves quality at lower memory. That enables more concurrent KV caches and fewer GPU swaps.
- Throughput validation: for the pilot footprint (2x H100), we estimate sustainable steady-state of ~4–5M tokens/day with p90 < 250ms if we get ~80% cache hit-rate on repeated contexts.
- Test plan: 1) synthetic load using representative prompt distribution (I can share the script), 2) 2-hour soak at 1.5x expected peak to validate autoscaling triggers, 3) capture token counts and latency percentiles.
- Risks: very long tails (multi-turn > 2k tokens) will increase average sequence length and push unit costs up — we'll track per-prompt token mix during the pilot.

I'll prepare a short runbook and the synthetic load script. Jordan / Marissa: let me know if you want the pricing spreadsheet updated with a specific quantization assumption (int8 vs int4) — that changes the lower bound by ~10–15%.

—Camila
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com
